map.：对照表按界（代）组织：新生界（2.58 Ma 至今）、中生界（252–66 M: : the reference is organized by era: Cenozoic (2.58 Ma to present), Mesozoic (252–66 Ma), Paleozoic (541–252 Ma), and Precambrian (over 541 Ma). Each system lists its age range, typical rocks, and index fossils — for example the Cambrian at 541–485 Ma (trilobites, the Chengjiang biota) and the Cretaceous at 145–66 Ma (the dinosaur extinction, early birds). The reference is local and needs no network.
map.：例：某剖面含三叶虫与笔石页岩 → 归入寒武系（541–485 Ma，古生界）；: : for example, a section with trilobites and graptolite shale belongs to the Cambrian System (541–485 Ma, Paleozoic); red sandstone with dinosaur fossils to the Cretaceous (145–66 Ma, Mesozoic); and human fossils with loess to the Quaternary (2.58 Ma to present, Cenozoic). Their spans are about 56 Ma, 79 Ma, and 2.58 Ma respectively, which lets you order them.
